about: Stages and timing for the facet-tune-up playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: review
stages.do: Review the filters on the top searches and categories, add the boost, bury, hide and always-show recommendations as findings, and agree which to make.

stages.name: qa
stages.do: Check each chosen facet change before anything is written: scope, facets both shown and hidden, clashes and running tests. Drop or change what fails.

skip_when.reason: the review found no facet change worth making.

stages.name: fix
stages.do: Plan the checked changes, update the rule that covers each page or create a new rule switched off, switch it on, each batch after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the review found no facet change worth making.

stages.name: measure
stages.do: Check the busiest changed facet rule paid off on the pages it covers, with the change and its live date from the hand-off file.

skip_when.reason: no facet change went live, so there is nothing to measure.
the fix stage was skipped, so nothing changed.

notes.measure_after_days: Days after the fix stage finishes (the facet rules went live) before the measure stage is due. change-impact-tracker needs about 14 days of data after a change for a verdict other than too early to tell.
notes.max_chosen: How many findings can be chosen at once. The review recommends several changes; each chosen one gets its own change file and plan in the fix stage, so each change is tied to its finding.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when an earlier stage had one of these outcomes, or with skipped: true when it was skipped).
